item: the Kubernetes manifests described a deployment that could not start
not_deployed: every run used a scratch namespace deleted on exit; the gocommerce namespace was never touched, and the drill refuses to apply if any rendered object still targets it
the_problem: k8s/configmap.yaml pointed at hosts named postgres, redis, elasticsearch and kafka. No object in the repository provided any of them: the stateful layer existed only in docker-compose.yml. Applying k8s/ produced eight services that could not reach a database, and nothing said so -- the YAML was valid and kubectl apply --dry-run=client passed.

what_was_added.k8s/data-tier: StatefulSets for PostgreSQL (WAL archiving, PITR archive volume), Redis (AOF persistence and an LRU bound), Elasticsearch and Kafka in KRaft, plus NetworkPolicies allowlisting which service may reach which store
what_was_added.deploy/overlays/production-managed-data: deletes all four StatefulSets and repoints every endpoint at managed instances, so adding an in-cluster tier does not silently redefine production as self-hosted single-node PostgreSQL
what_was_added.ops/k8s/render-postgres-init-configmap.s: generates the init ConfigMap from the same docker/postgres/init-databases.sh Compose uses, so the two cannot drift
what_was_added.ops/testing/data-tier-deploy.sh: the drill that produced this evidence
what_was_added.k8s/frontend.yaml: the shop, which had no container, no manifest and no Compose entry: applying k8s/ brought up nine APIs and nothing a shopper could open. nginx-unprivileged on 8080, read-only root, with the ingress routing /api to the gateway and everything else to the single-page app

checks: PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch and Kafka all become ready from the base manifests
the init script created five databases, each owned by its own least-privilege role, and each role reached its own database with the password from its Secret
a role cannot open another service's database
Redis, Elasticsearch and Kafka answer on the service names the ConfigMap publishes
all five migration Jobs complete against the tier
all ten Deployments start and pass their own readiness probes: api-gateway, auth, catalog, cart, search, order, analytics, recommendation, embedding and the frontend
a product is retrieved through catalog-service from inside the api-gateway pod, and the frontend serves its index page, so the cluster network, service DNS and the migrated schema all work

defects_found_that_were_in_committed_cod: Three of five migration Jobs crash-looped: they run the service's own image, so Spring builds the service's whole application context, but the Jobs carried none of the Secrets their Deployments carry. auth, catalog and order failed; analytics and recommendation happened to have no such beans and completed, which made it look like a per-service quirk. The documented release procedure would have blocked on kubectl wait for its full timeout. ops/testing/migration-job.sh missed this because it exports the credentials in the shell before running the jar: it tests the migrate profile, never the Job manifest's env wiring.

JwtProperties could not bind from environment variables, so auth-service could not start under Kubernetes or Docker Compose. It is a @ConfigurationProperties JavaBean, and a public getPrivateKey() made Spring's binder treat security.jwt.private-key as a bindable property; with SECURITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64 in the environment, relaxed binding made that prefix look populated, so the binder invoked the accessor partway through binding and hit its eager validation. Only auth-service, because only auth-service is given a private key. 41 platform-security tests passed throughout: every one binds from properties, never from the environment, which is the only form that triggers it. The four derived accessors are now named resolve*, and JwtPropertiesEnvironmentBindingTest binds through a real SystemEnvironmentPropertySource; restoring the old name reproduces the production message.

The Kafka StatefulSet advertised a hardcoded gocommerce namespace, which would have broken the pre-existing deploy/overlays/staging (namespace gocommerce-staging): the broker would advertise a DNS name that does not resolve there. Now built from the Downward API.

embedding-service could not start in Kubernetes. The manifest passed only EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME with no model on disk and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, so each pod would try to download BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 into a home directory it cannot write. The second half matters more: the download was unpinned, so the weights -- and therefore every embedding and every search result -- could change without a deploy, silently invalidating the evaluation evidence. The Dockerfile now fetches the weights at build time pinned to revision 5c38ec7c405ec4b44b94cc5a9bb96e735b38267a and verifies model.safetensors against sha256 3c9f31665447c8911517620762200d2245a2518d6e7208acc78cd9db317e21ad -- the same digest recorded in the search evaluation evidence -- so the build fails rather than shipping weights the evidence does not describe. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 stops a pod reaching for another.

frontend/src/api/apiBase.js read the API base as `VITE_API_BASE_URL || "http://localhost:8080"`. `||` treats an empty string as unset, so a same-origin deployment -- the configuration that lets one image serve every environment -- would have compiled localhost:8080 into the bundle and every shopper's browser would have called their own machine. Changed to `??`; the built bundle now contains zero occurrences of localhost:8080, asserted directly.
a_decision_made_explicit_rather_than_sil: auth-service's migration Job carries the JWT signing key. On least-privilege grounds it should not, but AuthService takes JwtIssuer as a constructor argument, so excluding the bean under the migrate profile cascades through the service and controller layer, and @Lazy would move key validation from startup to the first login. A malformed key failing a deploy is worth more than the narrower blast radius, particularly as the same pod already holds credentials that read password hashes. The reasoning is recorded in k8s/migrations/jobs.yaml.
defects_in_the_drill_itself_found_by_run: tr < /dev/urandom | head -c gets SIGPIPE, which pipefail turns into exit 141
ServiceAccounts were not applied, so Job pods stayed Pending while the Jobs read Running
seven-month-old service images were silently under test; the drill now refuses an image older than the source it claims to run, which is how the stale build was caught
that freshness checker dropped the UTC offset from Docker's timestamp and reported freshly built images as stale on a +05:30 machine

the freshness checker treated .DS_Store as source, so every image on a Mac was permanently stale; it now ignores what backend/.dockerignore already excludes, and reports an unreadable timestamp as a message rather than a stack trace

images were being built as `-t $s:latest` in zsh, where $s:l is the lowercase parameter modifier: the tag became <service>atest and <service>:latest silently kept an older build, while docker build reported success. Three services were affected and the freshness check is what caught it.
limits: One replica of each store: a single failure domain, no failover, and an upgrade window that stops all five databases at once. This is a startable deployment, not a resilient one.
Elasticsearch runs with security disabled, matching docker-compose. The NetworkPolicy is what limits access to it, and NetworkPolicies are not enforced on this cluster.
Kafka is one broker with replication factor 1: losing its volume loses undelivered events.
The production-managed-data overlay is rendered and checked, not deployed: it points at REPLACE_ME endpoints by design.

All nine services now start and pass readiness, and one request is served end to end. That is a start-up and connectivity proof, not a functional one: no checkout, search or payment flow is exercised in the cluster, and readiness says a process answered its own probe.
